title: Digital Plumber
description: Determine connectivity in a bidirectional graph of programs and pipes.
writeup:
## Approach

The input describes a set of programs connected by bidirectional communication pipes. Each line lists a program ID and the IDs it can directly communicate with. This forms an undirected graph.

## Part 1

To find how many programs are in the group containing program 0, we perform a graph traversal (DFS or BFS) starting from node 0. Every node reachable from 0 belongs to the same connected component. The size of this component is the answer to Part 1.

## Part 2

To determine how many groups exist in total, we iterate through all program IDs. For each unvisited node, we perform a traversal to mark all nodes in its connected component. Each traversal corresponds to one distinct group. Counting these traversals yields the total number of groups.

This puzzle is a straightforward application of graph connectivity and connected component detection.
